bg-21-01.hint: What shall we eat for lunch today?
bg-21-01.why: -(으)ㄹ까요? asks the listener's opinion or suggestion: 먹을까요?

bg-21-01.q: Suggest drinking coffee together using 같이 and 마실까요.
bg-21-01.why: -(으)ㄹ까요? asks the listener's preference or opinion politely.

steps.en: What shall we eat for lunch today?

ko: 친구에게 오늘 점심 같이 먹을까요라고 물었어요.
친구가 좋다고 해서 학생 식당으로 출발합시다라고 했어요.
en: After class ended, I was hungry.
I asked my friend, 'Shall we eat lunch together today?'
My friend agreed, so I said, 'Let's head to the student cafeteria.'

bg-21-01.q: What did the writer ask their friend after class?
options: Shall we eat lunch together today?
Shall we study at the library?
bg-21-01.why: The passage says '오늘 점심 같이 먹을까요라고 물었어요' (I asked, 'Shall we eat lunch together today?').

bg-21-01.q: Where did they decide to go?
bg-21-01.why: The text states '학생 식당으로 출발합시다라고 했어요' (I said, 'Let's head to the student cafeteria').

items: Propose activities together and ask opinions using -(으)ㄹ까요?
Use -(으)ㅂ시다 naturally when suggesting joint actions among peers

bg-21-02.hint: I will do it. Don't worry.
bg-21-02.why: -(으)ㄹ게요 expresses the speaker's personal promise to the listener.

bg-21-02.q: Promise to call someone tomorrow using 내일 and 전화할게요.
bg-21-02.why: -(으)ㄹ게요 conveys a direct promise from speaker to listener.

steps.en: I will call you tomorrow morning.
I will call you again tomorrow morning.

ko: 급한 일이면 문자 메시지를 남겨 주세요.
en: I am currently in a meeting, so it is difficult to talk on the phone.
I will contact you again after the meeting ends.
If it is urgent, please leave a text message.

bg-21-02.q: Why is the speaker unable to talk right now?
options: Because they are in a meeting
bg-21-02.why: The speaker says '지금은 회의 중이라서 통화가 어려워요' (I am currently in a meeting).

bg-21-02.q: What does the speaker promise to do after the meeting?
bg-21-02.why: The speaker promises '회의가 끝난 후에 다시 연락할게요' (I will contact you again after the meeting ends).

items: Make responsive promises and commitments to listeners using -(으)ㄹ게요
Restrict -(으)ㄹ게요 to first-person speaker commitments without using it for others

bg-21-03.hint: Would you like to watch a movie together on the weekend?
bg-21-03.why: -(으)ㄹ래요? asks the listener's intention or preference warmly.

bg-21-03.q: State your personal preference to rest at home using 집에서 and 쉴래요.

bg-21-03.hint: -(으)ㄹ게요 can only be used for the speaker (I), never for third persons (친구)! Use -ㄹ 거예요.
bg-21-03.why: Third-person future statements must use -(으)ㄹ 거예요, not -(으)ㄹ게요.

base.en: Do you want to watch a movie?

steps.en: Do you want to watch a movie on the weekend?
Do you want to watch a movie together this weekend?

ko: 친구에게 공원에서 같이 자전거 탈래요라고 물었어요.
친구도 좋다고 해서 같이 공원에 갔어요.
en: The weather is very nice on the weekend.
I asked my friend, 'Would you like to ride bicycles together in the park?'
My friend agreed too, so we went to the park together.

bg-21-03.q: What activity did the writer suggest?
bg-21-03.why: The text says '공원에서 같이 자전거 탈래요라고 물었어요' (I asked, 'Would you like to ride bicycles together in the park?').

bg-21-03.q: Did the friend agree to go?
options: Yes, they went to the park together
bg-21-03.why: The text says '친구도 좋다고 해서 같이 공원에 갔어요' (My friend agreed too, so we went to the park together).

items: Express personal choices and preferences using -(으)ㄹ래요
Inquire about friends' intentions and plans warmly with -(으)ㄹ래요?

bg-21-04.why: -(으)ㄹ게요 expresses a personal commitment directly to the listener.

bg-21-04.q: Volunteer to buy dinner for your friend using 제가 and 살게요.
bg-21-04.why: Use 제가 + [Verb-(으)ㄹ게요] to volunteer taking responsibility for an action.

bg-21-04.wrong: 선생님, 지금 다 같이 회의를 하읍시다.
answers: 선생님, 지금 다 같이 회의를 합시다.
선생님, 지금 다 같이 회의를 합시다
bg-21-04.hint: 하다 verbs attach -ㅂ시다 directly without 으: 하- + -ㅂ시다 → 합시다.

steps.en: Then I will buy the cold drinks.

ko: 민수 씨와 지민 씨가 저녁 약속을 정해요.
지민 씨가 좋다고 하면서 자기가 음료수를 살게요라고 약속했어요.
en: Minsu and Jimin are setting up dinner plans.
Jimin agreed and promised that she will buy the drinks.

bg-21-04.q: What food did Minsu propose eating?
bg-21-04.why: The text states '피자를 먹을까요라고 제안했어요' (He suggested, 'Shall we eat pizza?').

bg-21-04.q: What did Jimin promise to buy?
bg-21-04.why: The text states '자기가 음료수를 살게요라고 약속했어요' (She promised that she will buy the drinks).

items: Combine proposals, agreements, and personal commitments in one smooth plan-making conversation
